# ARS Rates

> Dollar to peso (USD to ARS) exchange rates in Argentina, updated every 15 minutes: dólar blue, MEP, CCL, official, wholesale (A3500), the crypto dollar, Western Union, Wise, Remitly, TapTap Send, Visa, Mastercard and American Express. Written in English for travelers and expats converting dollars to pesos.

All rates are pesos per 1 US dollar. Remittance and card rates are headline rates before fees. Rates are for information only.

## Current rates

- [rates.md](https://arsrates.com/rates.md): today's rates as plain text, refreshed every 15 minutes
- [current_rates.json](https://arsrates.com/static/data/current_rates.json): the same data as JSON
- [Prices and wages](https://arsrates.com/prices): monthly inflation (overall, food, transport, housing & utilities), average prices of beef, tomatoes, milk and bread in Greater Buenos Aires, average and minimum wages since Dec 2016 (INDEC, datos.gob.ar), the Big Mac (The Economist) and world food and meat prices (FAO Food Price Index), in pesos or converted to USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD and NZD at the monthly average Blue rate ([prices_wages.json](https://arsrates.com/static/data/prices_wages.json))
- [fx_rates.json](https://arsrates.com/static/data/fx_rates.json): daily EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD and NZD per US dollar since 2006 (ECB reference rates), used to show rates per other currencies
- [Rate history](https://arsrates.com/history): daily closing rates since 2006 (official), 2010 (CCL), 2011 (Blue) and 2018 (MEP) for Blue, MEP, CCL, official, Western Union, Visa, Mastercard and AMEX (from Aug 2025) ([rate_history.json](https://arsrates.com/static/data/rate_history.json); estimated values are listed under "estimated")

## Guides

- [How we get these rates](https://arsrates.com/methodology): sources for every rate, update times, and how the Mastercard and AMEX estimates work
- [Money Guide](https://arsrates.com/guide): paying by card vs. cash in Argentina, which card gets the best rate, and the safest ways to get pesos
- [Getting pesos with Western Union](https://arsrates.com/wu-guide): account setup, keeping fees down, locations that have cash, what to bring
- [Exchange houses and banks](https://arsrates.com/exchange-houses): where to change US dollars in greater Buenos Aires: exchange houses (casas and agencias de cambio) licensed by the Central Bank, updated weekly from the BCRA registry, and banks that change cash for non-customers (Banco Piano; Banco Nación at Ezeiza airport), with addresses, phones and hours
- [Western Union location finder](https://api.arsrates.com/wu-locations): search pickup locations by neighborhood, province or address, including WU's own branches
- [How to use ARS Rates](https://arsrates.com/how-to): how to read the rates table and use Quick comparison (what a 100,000-peso bill costs with each way to pay)
- [Rate emails and alerts](https://arsrates.com/features): free daily rate emails, and email alerts when a rate reaches a target

## Findings from our own data

Full write-ups: [What rate AMEX uses](https://arsrates.com/amex-rate-argentina), [Is Visa the MEP rate?](https://arsrates.com/visa-vs-mep), [Western Union vs changing cash](https://arsrates.com/western-union-vs-cash).

- American Express converts Argentine peso charges at the Central Bank's wholesale reference rate (Comunicación A 3500) from two business days before the charge, with no markup, and the charge shows its final dollar amount right away (AMEX used to charge the official rate and refund the difference later). Checked against about 200 real charges from October 2025 to October 2026: median difference 0.04%. That is typically 4-5% more pesos per dollar than Visa or Mastercard.
- Visa's rate is not the MEP rate. Visa follows the previous day's dólar MEP but ran roughly 5-7% below it during 2026 (median 6.5%), and about 4% below the A3500 rate.
- Mastercard's rate matches Visa's on weekdays.
- Visa, Mastercard and AMEX each set one rate per day for all card charges that day; market and money-transfer rates move during the day.
- Western Union's own branches ("Centros de Servicio") usually have cash; kioscos and payment agents often run out.
